title: Top open problems in mathematics ranked by LLM-assessed importance
lede: ProofAtlas ranks 500 open mathematics problems by importance, combining pairwise LLM comparisons in a reliability-weighted model, with P versus NP first and the Riemann Hypothesis second.

points: Importance weighs a resolution's significance, centrality in its field, reach across fields, fame and practical impact.
Judgments from OpenAI, Claude, GLM and DeepSeek models are weighted 1.00, 1.00, 0.95 and 0.90, which the site calls modelling choices.
Each entry gives the exact statement, why it matters, a sourced status note, related problems and a bootstrap rank range.
Dated status notes cover only 176 of the 500 entries, so the list is not a fresh review of the literature.

points.text: The top comment says the list mirrors press coverage, leading with Millennium Prize problems when Langlands matters more.
Commenters argue over whether an LLM ranking only echoes human consensus or adds any judgement of its own.
Asked which results would matter in practice, replies point to P versus NP and to one-way functions for cryptography.
Others flag gaps, such as status notes not updated since October and a missing elliptic-curve discrete log problem.
